title: Detection of circadian rhythms of clock gene mRNA in mouse lung tissue using slice cultures
author: Matsumura, Node, et al.
materials: High Capacity cDNA Reverse Transcription Kit

This section describes how to prepare the medium and dispense it into dishes. To streamline the process, prepare media for washing and re-culture for use after synchronizing stimulation with DEX as well as media for pre-culture at the same time. You can do this on the day of lung sectioning (Day 1 below) or the day before. If prepared the day before, store the medium at 4°C in a sealed container to prevent evaporation before use.1.Add FBS (Sigma SIGMA, Cat#173012) to the basal tissue slice culture media at a ratio of 1:10.Note: There is no problem using FBS used for cell culture.2.Dispense the FBS-supplemented culture media at 1.8 mL per non-treated 35 mm dish.Note: The number of dishes is twice that of the total needed in the experiment because they will be used for both pre-culture and re-culture.3.Dispense the basal culture media at 1.8 mL per 35 mm dish for washing.4.Put the inserts in the dishes with media for pre-culture (no need for washing and re-culture).Alternatives: If you use commercially available culture inserts (Merck Millipore, Cat# PICM0RG50) dispense 1.2 mL media per dish.Note: One slice on a culture insert of liver, pancreas, aorta, and white adipose tissue other than lung can also be cultured in this culture media.1,2 Therefore, this experimental protocol can be applied to tissues other than lung. However, note that we tested this protocol using liver, and the detection of circadian rhythm was more stable in lung than in liver.

In the steps below, RNA is extracted from the lung lysate using an RNeasy Mini Kit (Qiagen) and complementary DNA (cDNA) is synthesized using a High Capacity cDNA Reverse Transcription Kit (Thermo Fisher Scientific).24.To homogenize lung tissue completely, put the lysate prepared at the respective time points through a QIAshredder (Qiagen).25.Extract RNA using the RNeasy Mini kit following the manufacturer’s instructions (RNeasy Mini Handbook - (EN) - QIAGEN).26.Measure the concentration of extracted RNA in a spectrophotometer.27.Perform reverse transcription to prepare complementary DNA (cDNA) using 1.5 μg of purified RNA obtained as described above. The reaction solution composition and conditions follow the manufacturer’s protocol (Document Connect (thermofisher.com)).

steps.title: Prepare adult mice
steps.instruction: Estimate the number of mice required, obtain mice of a consistent age in weeks (by breeding or purchasing), house them on a 12‑h light/dark cycle at 23 °C with food and water ad libitum (or acclimate vendor mice for ≥1 week), and ensure they are ready for the experiment.

substeps.instruction: Estimate the number of mice needed according to the experimental plan.
Obtain mice of a consistent age in weeks (breed or purchase).
House mice in an animal facility with a 12‑h light/dark cycle, maintain room temperature at 23 °C, and provide food and water ad libitum.
If mice are purchased, acclimate them to these conditions for at least one week before use.
Note: mice of any age can be used, but breeding to obtain them takes ≥3 months.

steps.title: Prepare culture media
steps.instruction: Prepare basal tissue‑slice culture media, supplement with FBS, dispense into dishes for pre‑culture, washing, and re‑culture, and store if prepared the day before.

substeps.instruction: Add fetal bovine serum (Sigma, Cat# 173012) to the basal tissue‑slice culture media at a ratio of 1 : 10 (any cell‑culture‑grade FBS is acceptable).
Dispense the FBS‑supplemented media at 1.8 mL per non‑treated 35 mm dish. Prepare twice the number of dishes required for the experiment (they will be used for both pre‑culture and re‑culture).
Dispense basal (unsupplemented) culture media at 1.8 mL per 35 mm dish for washing steps.
Place culture inserts into the dishes containing the pre‑culture media (no washing or re‑culture needed for these dishes).
If using commercial culture inserts (Merck Millipore, Cat# PICM0RG50), dispense 1.2 mL media per dish instead of 1.8 mL.
Optional: Prepare all media on the day of lung sectioning (Day 1) or the day before; if prepared earlier, store sealed at 4 °C to prevent evaporation.

steps.title: Extract RNA and synthesize cDNA
steps.instruction: Homogenize lung lysates, extract total RNA, quantify it, and reverse‑transcribe 1.5 µg into cDNA using the specified kits.

substeps.instruction: Homogenize each lung lysate (collected at the scheduled time points) by passing it through a QIAshredder (Qiagen).
Extract total RNA using the RNeasy Mini Kit (Qiagen) following the manufacturer’s handbook (EN).
Measure RNA concentration with a spectrophotometer.

Set up reverse transcription using 1.5 µg of purified RNA with the High Capacity cDNA Reverse Transcription Kit (Thermo Fisher Scientific). Follow the kit’s recommended reaction composition and thermal cycling conditions (as detailed in the Thermo Fisher documentation).

steps.title: Quantify gene expression
steps.instruction: Perform RT‑qPCR, normalize to 18S‑rRNA, and analyze rhythmicity statistically.

substeps.instruction: Run RT‑qPCR for the clock genes of interest and for the reference gene 18S‑rRNA.
Normalize each gene’s Ct value to 18S‑rRNA and set the first time point of the wild‑type control to a value of 1 for comparative purposes.
Visually inspect expression profiles for rhythmic versus arrhythmic patterns.
Statistically test each time point using a t‑test to detect significant differences.
Optionally, use the Cosinor analysis tool (Refinetti) to evaluate the significance of rhythmicity.

description: In this protocol, tissue slices in culture are harvested at regular time intervals over a period of one or more days, RNA is extracted, and the expression levels of clock genes are measured to detect the circadian rhythm of the peripheral clock. This protocol repurposes and modifies the tissue slice culture method used for real-time measurement of the circadian bioluminescence rhythm of the luciferase-fused clock gene (e.g., Per2Luc,2) harbored by mice.1,2 The procedure described below is performed at a 6-hourly time point over two days. The duration and time point intervals can be changed, however, and should be set according to the purpose of your study. Hughes et al.3 will be helpful with your experiment design. However, note the number of tissue slices that can be prepared from one mouse and the time required to obtain them. To ensure a sufficient amount of RNA, about ten slices per time point are required. If slice collection takes too long, the viability of the slices decreases. In our experience, 4- to 8-h intervals for one to two days is practical. This protocol may be applied to any strain of mice. Here, mice with the C57BL/6 genetic background4 are used. In our experiments, preparing a sufficient number of slices from the lung of one mouse for a duplicate of ten time points in total (6-h intervals over a two-day time course) was successful. The protocol below shows the procedure for a time course of 2 days (10 time points) at 6-h intervals.
